evals.prompt: I'm deploying a Hono API to a serverless edge runtime where cold-start latency is the dominant cost. Show me how to construct the Hono application instance, choosing the most appropriate router for this deployment, and briefly explain why.
assertions: Constructs the app by passing an explicit router to the Hono constructor, e.g. new Hono({router: new LinearRouter()})
Selects LinearRouter (imported from "hono/router/linear-router") and justifies it by fastest init / no build step for cold start

evals.prompt: Using @hono/zod-openapi, add a GET /items/{id} endpoint that returns the item as JSON or a 404 problem-details response when it isn't found. Wire it into an OpenAPIHono router with a createRoute schema.
assertions: The handler is registered inline inside router.openapi(route, (c) => {...}) rather than extracted into a separate controller function
Every c.json() call passes an explicit literal status code (e.g. c.json(item, 200) and c.json(problem, 404)), never relying on an implicit 200

evals.prompt: Protect my Hono API so clients can't send huge request bodies and exhaust memory. I want a small global cap on all routes but a much larger allowance on the /upload route.
assertions: Uses the bodyLimit middleware imported from "hono/body-limit"
Sets maxSize as a byte value with a low global limit and a larger per-route maxSize applied specifically to the upload route

evals.prompt: I have a root Hono app, a /api/v1 router, and an /items leaf router mounted with .route(). The generated OpenAPI spec is missing all the /items routes. What is wrong and how do I fix the router composition?
assertions: Identifies that every router in the chain (root, intermediate, and leaf) must be OpenAPIHono, not plain Hono
States that a single plain Hono anywhere in the path drops its children's routes from the generated spec
